incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks customers (PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls)
incidents.vector: Buffer overflow in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication (Captive) Portal exposed to the public internet, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution as root (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3).
incidents.impact: Likely state-sponsored cluster CL-STA-1132 injected shellcode into nginx, deployed open-source tunneling tools (EarthWorm, ReverseSocks5), enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials, and systematically destroyed logs. CISA added the flaw to KEV and ordered federal mitigations by Saturday; first patches expected May 13.

incidents.vector: Tampered Daemon Tools installers (versions 12.5.0.2421-12.5.0.2434) distributed via the official Disc Soft website starting around April 8, embedding backdoors in core components that auto-execute at startup.
incidents.impact: Most infected systems received only a basic profiler, while a more advanced 'Quic RAT' was selectively deployed to government, science, manufacturing, and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand. Kaspersky observed Chinese-language elements in the malicious code; Disc Soft is investigating and the campaign remains active.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized possession and online publication of Alberta's official electoral list by an activist group (the Centurion Project) tied to a separatist political party.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, and other personal information of roughly three-fifths of Alberta's population were posted in a public, searchable database. The Republican Party of Alberta took the database down after Elections Alberta sued; police are investigating.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Exploitation of edge devices and n-day/zero-day vulnerabilities for initial access, followed by deployment of custom .NET backdoors (NetDraft), CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL/SNOWLIGHT, and a new Rust-based stager (SNOWRUST), with Impacket and PowerShell for AD reconnaissance.
incidents.impact: Long-term, low-noise access to government and related entities for credential theft and lateral movement. Active against South American governments since at least late 2024 and southeastern European governments through 2025; tooling overlaps with multiple other China-nexus clusters.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion; the World Leaks extortion group listed Mediaworks and published internal files.
incidents.impact: Leaked documents include meeting notes in which content directors said they would contact Moscow for help publishing anti-Ukraine content, exposing apparent Hungary-Russia propaganda coordination. Mediaworks has filed a lawsuit against a publication that covered the leak.

incidents.vector: Compromised admin account; the attacker reduced the delay on admin actions to zero in order to execute malicious transactions instantly across multiple integrated blockchains.
incidents.impact: Approximately $5 million in crypto-assets stolen in a single, coordinated operation.

incidents.vector: Specific intrusion vector not disclosed; Moldova's Cybersecurity Agency adjunct director said no ransom was demanded and did not exclude Russian involvement.
incidents.impact: Roughly 30% of CNAM data was stolen and/or had to be restored from backups, including personal and financial information on essentially every adult in Moldova plus financials of all private medical providers under the national insurance scheme. Payments and medical services have continued normally.

incidents.vector: Threat actor gained unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source code repository; access path and adversary not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no evidence the source-code release/distribution process was affected, but a security-vendor source-code breach can map control locations and detection logic, advantaging future attackers. Forensics and law enforcement engaged; full scope still unconfirmed.

incidents.victim: Schemata (U.S. Department of Defense training contractor)
incidents.vector: Multi-tenant API endpoints lacked authorization checks; a low-privilege account could enumerate cross-tenant user, course, and document data via normal browser-session API calls, with some routes appearing write-enabled.
incidents.impact: Exposed Army field manuals on explosive ordnance handling, naval maintenance training marked confidential, and hundreds of records linking U.S. service members to bases and training enrollments. Schemata says it has no evidence of third-party exploitation; remediated May 1 after a 150-day disclosure process with researcher Strix.

incidents.vector: Voice phishing impersonating IT support drives employees to SSO-themed adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) pages that capture credentials and live session tokens; persistence is established by registering attacker-controlled MFA devices (Genymobile Android emulators, QEMU) and suppressing security email notifications.
incidents.impact: Single authenticated identity-provider session enables rapid lateral movement across the victim's entire SaaS estate without touching endpoints, supporting fast data theft and extortion. Activity has been observed continuously since October 2025 and was still active in late April.

incidents.vector: TP-Link Archer AX21 routers compromised through CVE-2023-1389 to build a Mirai-variant DDoS/DNS-amplification botnet. The botnet was operated using SSH keys belonging to the CEO of Brazilian DDoS-mitigation firm Huge Networks, whose infrastructure had been compromised in a January 2026 intrusion.
incidents.impact: Sustained DDoS waves against small Brazilian ISPs (10-60 second attacks per IP prefix, four parallel processes per host). Huge Networks engaged third-party forensics and rotated keys; the CEO denies involvement and attributes the activity to a competitor exploiting the breach.

incidents.vector: Compromise of an on-premises Microsoft Exchange email server, part of a broader 2026 campaign that has hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers worldwide.
incidents.impact: Cuban diplomats' email inboxes were exfiltrated, providing China visibility into Cuba's understanding of the U.S. naval blockade.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company / Delta Dental of New York
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (MOVEit / Cl0p, mid-2023)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of the MOVEit Transfer zero-day (CVE-2023-34362) in mid-2023 to access DDIC and DDNY's MOVEit servers and exfiltrate large volumes of files.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included names, addresses, SSNs, driver's license numbers, financial account information, and patient health information. NYDFS imposed a $2.25 million penalty on April 30, 2026 for inadequate incident response and late breach notification under 23 NYCRR Part 500.

incidents.vector: Social engineering of two DigiCert tech-support employees, who were tricked into running a malicious .SCR (Windows screensaver) file. CrowdStrike Falcon was misconfigured on one host and not connected to its central management server, letting the attacker maintain access for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attacker harvested 'initialization codes' from approved EV-certificate orders and obtained 27 EV code-signing certificates, which were then used to sign Zhong Stealer payloads tied to cryptocurrency-theft campaigns. DigiCert has revoked all 60 EV certificates issued during the compromise window.

incidents.vector: March 2026 cyberattack; specific access vector and threat actor not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hasbro delayed publication of its Q1 2026 financial results because shipping, invoicing, and financial-consolidation systems were still being restored, signalling significant operational and financial disruption from the original incident.

incidents.vector: Data theft via ShinyHunters' broader 2026 campaign, which has also compromised Zara, 7-Eleven, Udemy, and Medtronic; specific access vector at Carnival not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 7.5 million Carnival customers leaked online by the group following the original 2026 breach.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion of internal corporate systems discovered April 13, 2026.
incidents.impact: Itron disclosed the breach and says the incident has been resolved; cyber insurance is expected to cover most costs. Customer-facing impact details have not been published.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment with double-extortion data theft.
incidents.impact: SafePay leaked Favelle Favco's stolen data online after the company did not pay the ransom; operational impact not disclosed.

incidents.vector: Likely ransomware; specific vector not disclosed by the county.
incidents.impact: Harrison County, one of West Virginia's largest counties, disclosed a cybersecurity incident; recovery is ongoing and operational impact details remain limited.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion that diverted funds during a foreign debt repayment scheduled to Australia.
incidents.impact: Approximately $2.5 million was siphoned from a sovereign debt repayment. Sri Lanka has asked Australian law enforcement to assist the investigation; recovery and attribution remain outstanding.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach exposed records of medical-data volunteers; data subsequently appeared for sale on the Alibaba marketplace.
incidents.impact: Personal information of roughly half a million people who volunteered their medical data to the UK Biobank was offered for sale online, with potential downstream privacy and research-trust harms.
